title: lp_doc v2.0 — the LP-HTML v8 content model (grades 6-12)
description: THE one content model for a Rumi 6-12 lesson plan. Unifies senior_lp_schema_v1 (provenance / verbatim SLO / subject packs) with the render_lp_html.js block shape (say / board / watch / diagram). The lp_doc JSON is the ARTEFACT OF RECORD; the PDF is a cache. Spine is the FDE lesson diary (Objectives, Introduction, Development, Activity, Conclusion, Homework) — see PLAN_lp_v8_html_2026-08-30.md D1. What varies by lp_type is the INTERNALS of development/activity, never the spine (D2). Every string may carry inline $...$ KaTeX and \ce{...} mhchem.

lesson_id.description: Stable key, e.g. PK_G7_GSCI_CH1_PHOTOSYNTHESIS. Also the cache key for the rendered PDF.

lint_profile.description: 'full' = every pedagogy gate applies (the only value a teacher-facing LP may carry). 'smoke' = a deliberately tiny fixture that proves the renderer; word budgets and FDE-completeness are skipped and lint prints a loud banner. Never ship a 'smoke' doc to a teacher.

provenance.description: Every factual claim in the LP must trace to this page range. printed != pdf; the offset differs per book and is recorded in each 01_page_truth/*.json.

book_stem.description: e.g. grade_7_general_science — the page-truth corpus key

medium.description: Language of INSTRUCTION. Textbook quotations stay in the book's own language regardless (LP_DESIGN_RULES §5).

printed_pages.description: What the teacher sees printed on the page, e.g. '11' or '20-21'

pdf_pages.description: Index into the source PDF, e.g. '13'

source_quality_flags.description: Known defects in the source the LP must not propagate.

brand.description: The DEPLOYMENT's brand — whose name the teacher reads on the page. OPTIONAL, and its absence is meaningful: with no brand the page carries NO brand text at all (white-label). Render-law 13: the authoring house is not the deployment brand, and no internal brand — the company's, the product's or a partner's — may appear as content. lint_lp.js FAILS (BRANDLEAK) on any other brand's name found in the document's strings.

name.description: e.g. 'NIETE Teaching Assistant'. Printed in the hero kicker and the support-page footer.

primary_hex.description: The brand's primary colour, e.g. NIETE navy-slate '#333748'. Colours the footer brand mark.

chapter_title.description: The chapter's NAME, when the book prints one separately from `chapter` (which is normally 'Ch. 6 · Stoichiometry'). Optional, additive: it only enriches the page footer.

version.description: ISO date this lp_doc was authored/revised, e.g. '2026-08-30'. Printed in the page footer as v<date> so a teacher and a reviewer can tell two copies apart. OPTIONAL — the renderer NEVER invents one: an undated doc simply carries no version.

slo.description: NEVER invented. FBISE examines SLOs, not textbooks. R2: the objective goes at the top, always.

code.description: e.g. B-10-R-10. null when the book prints an outcome with no code — say so rather than inventing one.

source_page.description: Printed page the outcome is quoted from.

cognitive_level.description: FBISE buckets: K=Knowledge, U=Understanding, A=Application (apply/analyse/evaluate/create). Paper weighting 30/50/20.

assessment_status.description: Formative SLOs are taught but EXCLUDED from the board exam.

success_criterion.description: The outcome restated in exam terms: 'by the end you can answer a 4-mark SRQ on X'.

lp_type.description: Decides the Development/Activity INTERNALS, never the spine. STEM-1 phenomenon-first, STEM-2 I-do/we-do/you-do, STEM-3 investigation, LL-* languages, SS-* social studies, RECALL recall-floor, GEN-6-8 the general middle-school shape.

period_minutes.description: THE MINUTES RULE (L3 ask 4): warmup.minutes plus the minutes of EVERY section — homework included, normally 1-2 — must equal this exactly. lint_lp.js enforces it. A teacher counted 5+8+17+7=37 against a labelled 40 and wrote it up.

board_weight.description: e.g. 'FBISE SSC-I · ~8 marks'. null for grades 6-8 (FBISE's examining remit starts at SSC).

materials.description: Physical things only. Zero-materials alternatives belong in the block that needs them.

warmup.description: Just-in-time acceleration, not remediation (TNTP). 2 prerequisite + 1 spaced, ANSWERS PRINTED.

layout.description: 'half' puts the W band beside the FIRST section when that section is also 'half' — the introduction. Saves ~50px on page 1.

from.description: For kind=spaced: which earlier chapter/page it retrieves.

objectives.description: Section O. First entry is normally the verbatim SLO restated as a pupil-facing 'can do'; locally-added application objectives must SAY they are locally added.

sections.description: The FDE spine, in order. lint (profile=full) requires exactly introduction, development, activity, conclusion, homework.

title.description: Override for the printed bar label. Defaults to the localized section name.

layout.description: 'half' pairs this section with the NEXT consecutive 'half' section into one two-column band, each keeping its own lettered bar. Use it for short tail sections (conclusion + homework) — it is the single biggest space saving on page 1. A lone trailing 'half' renders full width.

page2.description: Support page. Explicitly NOT read aloud in class.

board_final.description: A — the board at the END of the lesson: the diagram in final state plus the order to draw it in.

model_answers.description: B — every practice item answered in full, grouped by tier/part.

mistakes.description: C — what pupils actually write, and the exact question you ask back. Naming a misconception is not addressing it.

differentiation.description: D — one concrete instruction each. Never narrative.

exam_bank.description: E — the exam surface. lint requires mcq >= 2, srq and erq_skeleton for grades 9-12.

answer.description: The correct option, as its letter (A/B/C/D) or its full text.

distractor_codes.description: One short misconception code per WRONG option, in option order. A distractor that encodes nothing is a wasted distractor (EEF diagnostic questions).

srq.description: One short-response question in exact board phrasing + a bullet mark scheme (the 50% band).

erq_skeleton.description: Headings + marks per part. Not a model essay.

marks_total.description: L3 ask 7. Omit and the total is the sum of the parts; lint warns when a stated total disagrees with that sum.

how_marked.description: One line on what earns and what loses the mark.

homework_key.description: F — the homework worked through in FULL, not 'see answer key'.

next_period.description: G — one line, with the SLO code where there is one.

not_going.description: G — what NOT to teach yet, and why. Stops the LP being over-taught into next period's content.

coaching_lookfor.description: H — the observable a Digital Coach observer would look for in this lesson.

one_screen.description: The ~200-word WhatsApp message body: objective -> 1 prerequisite item + answer -> worked example <=5 steps -> 3 practice items + answers -> misconception -> exit question. The PDF is the attachment. Front-loads practice because the END of a structured lesson is what gets cut (MDPI 16:5:699).

notes.description: Author-side record (L3 ask 1). Distinct from provenance.source_quality_flags, which is ONLY for defects in the printed source. These are about the LESSON: what it had to add, what the book got wrong, and what the pages could not give.

supplied.description: Facts the LP supplies that the book never states, each with the page checked. A supplied fact that is not declared here is indistinguishable from an invention.

defects.description: A missing answer key, an unused given, an outcome the exercise does not cover. LP_DESIGN_RULES §5 makes these the PREFERRED basis for a lesson, so they must survive into the artefact.

gaps.description: What the page range could not give at all.

needs_human_review.description: Skill gate G5c (L3 ask 2). Islamiat and سیرت content is NEVER served on-demand. A boolean the serving path branches on — not a substring match against a free-text array. `lint_lp.js --auto-send` FAILS on a doc with this set.

ur_overlay.description: THE URDU TOGGLE (operator decision 2026-08-30: English author + Urdu toggle, not side-by-side). Keys are RFC-6901 JSON Pointers into THIS document; values are the Urdu string that replaces the English one at render time under `--lang ur`. Structure never changes — only instruction strings swap, so an lp_doc has one shape and two renderings. Books whose medium is already 'ur' are authored in Urdu directly and carry no overlay. WHAT MAY NOT BE OVERLAID (lint enforces): /slo/text_verbatim (the printed outcome, quoted), anything under /page2/exam_bank (the exam is in the book's language), and the text of any `board` block (board text follows the exam). Textbook quotations inside a paragraph stay in the book's language too — overlay the instruction around them, not the quote.

revisions.description: Append-only edit log. Edits arrive as whitelisted JSON-Patch, re-lint, re-render.

diagram_spec.description: Handed verbatim to diagrams/index.js -> renderDiagram(spec) -> SVG string. L2 owns the renderer and the per-type sub-schemas; L1 only guarantees `type` exists and passes the rest through untouched.

alt.description: Screen-reader / fallback text. Also what lint reads when the diagram cannot be rendered.

block.description: One renderable unit. Exactly one vocabulary — the renderer switches on `type` and nothing else.

id.description: Optional label so an `ask.closed_by` can point here.

oneOf.description: A line the teacher says out loud. The only scripted part (semi-scripting; scripting correlates slightly NEGATIVELY with outcomes).

id.description: Optional label so an `ask.closed_by` can point here.

oneOf.description: A question the teacher asks, with what a good answer contains. M2: middle/high teachers want the QUESTIONS, not a script.

look_for.description: What a correct/promising answer contains. Not the answer to read out.

hook.description: true = this is the lesson's provocation (M3). Exactly one per LP, in the introduction.

closed_by.description: The `id` of the later block that ANSWERS this hook (L3 ask 3). The most repeated teacher complaint across v7 was an opening question the lesson never closes; naming the closing beat is what lets lint check it.

oneOf.description: The 'don't do this yet' / misconception caution.

misconception.description: true = this states a named pupil misconception (lint requires >=1 in development).

oneOf.description: What must be left visible on the board.

title.description: Overrides the printed "Key points" label. Pass "" to print no label at all — e.g. a homework list, which is a list of tasks and not a set of key points.

oneOf.description: WE DO — same type, 1-2 steps blanked. Fading beats fixed examples.

answer.description: What the blanked steps come to. Required by lint — every closed item is solved.

oneOf.description: YOU DO — graded items, ANSWERS ALONGSIDE. The heart of the plan.

mode.description: Renders the GUIDED PRACTICE / INDEPENDENT PRACTICE tag the v7-1 teachers recognised.

tier.description: Difficulty. NOT the cognitive level — see `level`.

level.description: FBISE cognitive level, weighted ~30/50/20 across a paper (L3 ask 5). Teachers who liked LP2 said so because it followed K/U/A.

oneOf.description: The two side-by-side cards from v7-1: a simplified starter and an early-finisher stretch.

Two blocks side by side as CARDS. This is the v7-1 Support/Extension pattern generalised, and it is how a figure sits beside its key points without either shrinking. D4 forbids side-by-side BODY TEXT, so lint rejects a split containing `paragraph`, `practice`, `worked_example` or `faded_example`, and rejects nested splits.

ratio.description: Fraction of the width the LEFT column takes.

oneOf.description: A REAL figure from the book, used as 'as in your book, p.N' reference art. Any figure that must be labelled correctly for the exam is redrawn as SVG instead.

src.description: Repo-relative path to the crop. Never an absolute /Users path. OPTIONAL when `ref` is given (L3 ask 6): the figure-locator pass may not have run yet, so the renderer falls back to the caption/legend text and REPORTS the missing crop rather than failing.

legend.description: One line telling the teacher how to READ the figure.

oneOf.description: Display maths. Body text carries inline $...$ instead.
Display chemistry (mhchem). `tex` is the INSIDE of \ce{...}.
